correctness.rationale: All squared singular values are obtained from exact orthogonal angular-frequency images and explicitly normalized Gaussian gamma integrals, with n=0 checked separately. A Poisson-tail identity resolves three terms; the central limit theorem plus exponential tails establishes the full boundary and counting limits. The p<1 and p>1 mass laws follow from separate bulk and edge estimates; at p=1 a pointwise square-root inequality plus Poisson large deviations proves the nontrivial additive coefficient 1+I_1. Independent quadratures and finite Poisson calculations gave 108 supplementary assertions. Finite checks are not substituted for all-T proof.

originality.rationale: Published mathematical findings were searched by object, aliases, tail parameters, and Schatten spectra. Three close published full results were read. The closest disk semi-commutator has the same known Gaussian product but no bulk population and does not state the exact big-Hankel spectrum or the critical mixed trace coefficient. A related Landau interlevel transfer and exterior Laurent Hankel family also have different spectral formulas. Broader Fock literature supplies general criteria, not the exact combined theorem in inspected text. Risk from incomplete Qin and other broad old treatments is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The hard-disk truncation of the anti-analytic coordinate is a canonical simple compact Fock Hankel family motivated by semiclassical Toeplitz/Hankel quantization. The theorem determines an exact infinite singular multiset, a sharp operator norm and counting profile, and a nontrivial phase change at p=1: an order-T bulk and a sqrt(T)-wide order-sqrt(T) edge contribute simultaneously to the trace. The equality of the edge CDF with a known disk-Toeplitz profile is acknowledged, but that profile alone omits the new mixed Schatten behavior. The result is a natural spectral stability fact rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
